title: Rollout Causal Explorer and Shadow Replay Lab
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a Console feature set that lets PMs and SREs run causal comparisons between rollout cohorts (canary vs baseline), replay shadow traffic into variants for divergence analysis, and surface actionable auto-rollback recommendations. This ticket covers UX flows, backend telemetry hooks, and an experimental replay runner (shadow lab) to simulate variant behavior against production traces without affecting live traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-route cohort diffs (latency P50/P95, error rate, token-cost delta) for any active rollout within 5s of data availability.
A shadow-replay runner can accept a trace batch and replay it to a variant in a sandbox mode; results are captured and diffed against baseline within the Console UI.
Auto-rollback advisor surfaces an aggregated risk score and suggested rollback action when a variant breaches configurable thresholds (latency, error-rate, quality regression).
Telemetry events (trace links, cohort_id, variant_id, replay_id) are emitted and documented; each replay has an immutable linkable artifact in the Console.
notes: Design intent: emphasize causal attribution — separate traffic-driven divergence (routing/capacity) from model-quality regressions (statistical diff on outputs).
Backend must support trace-linked sampling for replay; consider using the existing trace store ingest (ENG-28501) and adding a replay queue with resource isolation to protect runtime pools.
We prioritized developer ergonomics: 'replay-to-variant' should be a single button from a trace or cohort comparison panel.
